text:
Marta: :rotating_light: incident-bot detected a large spike hitting /v1/generate and /v1/batch from many short-lived API keys. 500% traffic increase in last 10m, error rate up (5xx and 429s). Looks like scraper + credential stuffing combo. Paging SRE oncall.
Sukh: I'm on it. Can you paste the incident-bot digest and any quick counters?
Marta: incident-bot summary: 
```
alert: high-req-rate
routes: /v1/generate, /v1/batch
sources: multiple us-west/us-east/eu regions
top-useragents: "python-requests/2.*", "curl/7.*", "botify/*"
top-ip-counts: 120k unique ips, heavy reuse
anomalies: many new api_keys created last 2h
```
Also seeing many login attempts to /v1/auth: suspicious patterns, parallel spikes from same ASNs.
InfraBot: Auto-mitigation suggestions: 1) enforce per-key rate-limit 2) geo fallback for high-volume countries 3) disable anonymous batch endpoints. Recommend manual apply.
Chantal: Agreed. Quick plan: (A) tighten per-key QPS to 5 for new keys, (B) add short-term global burst window to cut sustained abuse, (C) enable WAF rule to block headers matching known scraper UAs, (D) enable geo shape for top offending countries.
Sukh: I'll take (A) and (B) now. Marta, can you coordinate (C) with Tom and (D) with infra? Alex (CS) can you flag any paying customers hitting errors? We need to avoid SLA breaches.
Alex (CS): On it. I already reached out to two customers with heavy traffic. Early signals: one enterprise had retries but no critical failures yet. I'll compile list of affected API keys and owners.
Tom (Security): For WAF, please give me the UA patterns and any header fingerprints. I can push a temporary blocklist and a challenge for JS-capable agents.
Marta: UA list in the digest. Also seeing unusual Accept-Encoding combos and missing referer headers. Example: `User-Agent: python-requests/2.24.0` and `X-Custom-Session: null` repeated.
Sukh: Executing live changes. Applying per-key QPS=5 for keys created in last 3h via admin API. Command I'm running:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.local/keys/bulk-update \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"filter":"created_after:$(date -d\"3 hours ago\" +%s)","rate_limit":{"qps":5,"burst":10}}'
```
Applying now — will monitor error rates.
InfraBot: Action accepted: rate-limits applied to 12.3k keys. Expected reduction: ~48% QPS.
Chantal: Next, reduce batch endpoint exposure for unauthenticated/anonymous clients: `feature.batch_public = false` toggle. That will protect against mass scraping of long outputs. Marta, deploy that toggle?
Marta: Toggling now in config: `feature.batch_public = false` (rolling deploy).
Tom (Security): WAF rule ready. Sample rule to block UA regex: `^(python-requests|curl|botify)\/` and challenge JS for others. Applying with immediate-block for UA hits > 20 req/min per IP.
```
# wafctl pseudo
wafctl add-rule --name "scraper-ua-block" --match "ua_regex:^(python-requests|curl|botify)/" --action block
wafctl add-rule --name "suspect-rate-challenge" --match "rate>20/min/ip" --action challenge
```
Applying now.
Sukh: Quick telemetry: after rate-limits and batch toggle, aggregate QPS down ~35% in 60s, 5xx trending down. Still seeing distributed credential attempts to /v1/auth though. We'll add stricter login throttling: per-account throttle and global captcha challenge for suspicious flows.
Alex (CS): Notifying affected paid accounts in parallel. One customer reported repeated 429s for legit jobs. Which keys are we throttling? Need to whitelist top-tier customers.
Marta: Whitelist exec: keys with tag `tier:enterprise` are excluded from the new per-key QPS. We only applied to keys created in last 3h. If someone legit got affected, tell me which key and I will lift.
Tom (Security): I'm also seeing a credential-stuffing signal: many failed auths followed by success from unusual IP clusters. Recommend blocking or rate-limiting auth attempts per account to 5 per 10 minutes and forcing cooldown.
Sukh: Implemented auth throttle: `auth.attempts.window=600s, max_attempts=5`. Also enabled exponential backoff on failed attempts.
InfraBot: Metrics update: total QPS -44% from peak, 5xx reduced by 70%, 429s remain elevated but falling. WAF blocked ~1.2M requests in last 10m.
Chantal: Good progress. Next steps: (1) Continue monitoring 30m, (2) capture top 500 API keys hitting limits and hand off to CS for owner contact, (3) gather full packet/log samples for security team, (4) prepare canary rollback plan for any recent config changes if we see regressions.
Sukh: On-call handoff in 20m to Marcus. I'll create followup ticket with all mitigations we applied and exact commands/logs.
Marta: Alex, please compile customer impact report (keys, regions, error rates) and tag support priority.
Alex (CS): Will do. Expect initial report in 10m.
Tom (Security): Keep WAF rules temporal (30-60m) and gather false-positive signals. I'll also add low-level heuristics for header anomalies.
Marta: Summary of live mitigations applied: 
- Per-key QPS=5 for keys created in last 3h (whitelisted enterprise tags)
- Batch public endpoints disabled
- WAF UA regex blocking + rate-challenge rules
- Auth attempt throttling (5 per 10m) + exponential backoff
- Geo-shaping applied to top offending regions (soft-throttle)
Impact: aggregate QPS down ~44%, 5xx down 70%, paid customer impact minimal so far (one enterprise saw retries).
Sukh: Will leave a cookbook snippet in the ticket for rollback:
```
# rollback snippet
# undo per-key update
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.local/keys/bulk-update \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"filter":"created_after:$(date -d\"3 hours ago\" +%s)","rate_limit":null}'
# re-enable batch if needed
configctl set feature.batch_public true
# remove waf rules
wafctl remove-rule --name "scraper-ua-block"
wafctl remove-rule --name "suspect-rate-challenge"
```
Marta: Marcus (next oncall) — please pick this up at handoff, confirm the WAF metrics/false positives, and coordinate with CS for any customer escalations.
Sukh: Handing off in 15m. Leaving alerts: error-rate > 5% sustained, paid-customer-errors > 1%.
Alex (CS): Report: initial 45 keys belonged to paid customers, all contacted, two requested immediate whitelist and had reduced throughput — we already whitelisted 1 enterprise key, working on second.
Tom (Security): I'll continue log collection and correlate with ASN blocks. If we see credential stuffing succeed for any enterprise account, we escalate to account security and require rotation.
Marta: Thanks everyone. I'll close this thread once Marcus confirms stabilization and the mitigation ticket is complete. :white_check_mark:
